_note: E3 inter-rater fixture — NEUTRAL, representative construct×leaf set (NOT rigged to pass). Deliberately mixes obvious-D, obvious-T, obvious-J leaves with ~5 genuinely-ambiguous ones (reading-grade score, follows-REST, survey-score, tone, blast-radius) where honest rater disagreement is expected. Raters classify each leaf D/T/J from the rubric ALONE (no skill-priming, no author gold). 6 constructs × 4 leaves = 24 items.

rubric.D: deterministic-measurable — a number a tool/script computes directly (e.g. coverage %, latency ms, CVE count), mappable to [0,1].
rubric.T: typeable/observable — a categorical fact you can classify or inventory by looking (e.g. present/absent, yes/no, which-category), no judgment call.
rubric.J: bounded-calibrated judgment — used ONLY when you can state why there is NO deterministic (D) or observable (T) method; the value requires a human/LLM judgment against a rubric.

items.leaf: unit-test line-coverage % of the changed lines
cyclomatic complexity of the changed functions
a PR description is present (yes/no)
how clearly the change communicates its intent to a future reader
5xx error rate over the last 24h
p99 request latency in milliseconds
an on-call engineer's felt confidence that the system is stable
a monitoring dashboard exists for the service (yes/no)
count of spelling/grammar errors
a table of contents is present (yes/no)
whether the tone is appropriate for the intended audience
Flesch-Kincaid reading-grade-level score
a documented rollback plan exists (yes/no)
percentage of config keys changed in this deploy
the reviewer's judgment of the blast-radius if it fails
the change is behind a feature flag (yes/no)
voluntary attrition rate over the quarter
average score on the anonymous engagement survey
a manager's read of the room during standups
number of team social events held this quarter
number of endpoints
endpoints follow REST resource-naming conventions (yes/no)
how elegant/intuitive the naming feels to a new consumer
the API is versioned (yes/no)
